items.title: Compromised jscrambler 8.14.0 npm Release Drops Rust Infostealer During Install
items.description: The jscrambler npm package was compromised, and simply installing its 8.14.0 release runs an infostealer on your machine. Published on July 11, 2026, the malicious version carries a preinstall hook that drops and executes a native binary, one build each for Windows, macOS, and Linux. items.title: New Ghostcommit Attack Hides Malicious Prompts in Images to Exploit AI Agents
items.description: A novel supply chain attack called “Ghostcommit” that conceals prompt-injection instructions within PNG images to bypass AI code reviewers and trick coding agents into leaking secrets such as .env files. The ASSET Research Group demonstrated that a pull request containing an explicit, plain-text instruction to exfiltrate a repository’s .env file is caught immediately by LLM-based […] The post…

items.title: 'Ghostcommit' hides prompt injection in images to fool AI agents, steal secrets
items.description: A PNG hiding a prompt injection could steal your repo's secrets, researchers demonstrate. The technique, dubbed 'Ghostcommit,' slipped past AI code reviewers CodeRabbit and Bugbot, which never open image files at all, then convinced a coding agent to read a repo's .env and write every secret into the code as a list of numbers. items.title: Dell BIOS Flaw Lets Attackers Recover Admin Passwords From SPI Flash in Milliseconds
items.description: A critical flaw in how Dell stores BIOS administrator and user passwords allows full password recovery from a flash dump in milliseconds, with no brute force required. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-40639 (DSA-2026-197), stems from a broken XOR encryption scheme rather than a proper cryptographic hash.
